Commentary.Commentary: Just 14 to win then. Can England pick up a wicket or two and salvage some pride? Not much of it left anyways...

Once again, Roach was the architect of the destruction. He came out firing after Tea and sent the middle and lower middle order packing, moving the ball like a hoop. Cannot say the English batsmen played bad strokes. They were just consumed by some fiery pace bowling. Holder continues his meteoric rise, grabbing another 4-fer. And yes, spare a thought for the 20-year old Alzarri Joseph, who is fighting a personal battle. He got the big wicket of Joe Root and then Denly.

Unbelievable. For the third time in 4 innings, Windies have blown the English away. A deficit of 119 was always going to be difficult to erase without losing much wickets but England lost 8 before they could get into the lead. We might have even witnessed an innings defeat, had Campbell taken the catch of Stokes earlier.

OUT! Slower ball, chipped in the air and taken! Holder has 4. The slower ball, at 122 kph, fuller in length, Anderson is foxed by the change in pace, as he backs away and looks to go inside out. He is early into the shot and just spoons the ball in the air. Alzarri Joseph charges in from mid on, keeps his eyes on the ball and dives in front to take a wonderful catch. 14 RUNS NEEDED FOR A 2-0 SERIES LEAD!
A bouncer to end the over, Anderson ducks.

DROPPED, FOUR! Roach had a chance to take his 5th. A full toss outside off, Curran mistimes his swipe back to the bowler. The ball dips onto Roach who tries to change his followthrough and take it low to his left but the ball bursts through his palms and just misses the stumps at the other end. Roston Chase starts to chase but comes second.
Backs away, Roach follows him, digs in a bouncer, Curran swings hard and swats it tennis-like through mid-wicket for a couple.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
Around off, punched towards cover.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full and wide outside off, Sam swings hard and miscues it over point. There is a man in the deep but he cannot get there. A single taken.
Comes down the track, Holder shortens the length, Sam adjusts and pushes it wide of mid off. Does not run.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Landed outside off, Curran slashes hard but misses.
Full and around middle, watchfully pushed towards cover.
Another outswinger, JA looks to drive but misses.
Another booming outswinger, Jimmy looks to defend but misses again.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball.
Full and around off, Anderson looks to defend but the ball swings away past the outside edge.
Superb yorker. Full and straight. Anderson looks to flick and is gone for all money. But just as the ball looks to sneak beneath the bat, the willow comes down to push the ball away.
Jimmy Anderson is the last man in.

OUT! Another LBW! 9 down! Roach gets 4. Perfect ball to a tail-ender. Keep a short leg and a silly point, instilling the thought of a short ball in his mind, then bowl a full ball. Broad picks it late, looks to flick but is late. Is hit on the pads and Roach appeals. Umpire Gaffaney raises his finger in a flash. Broad walks across to Curran to chat regarding the review and after a brief discussion, is sent back.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.
Outside off, punched through the covers again for a couple.
FOUR! HANDSOME! ENGLAND INTO THE LEAD NOW! Full and outside off, Curran leans into this one and drives it through the covers!

Another LBW shout, but not out. Full and around leg stump, swinging down, Broad gets across to flick but misses. Is hit on the pads but that was going down leg. The batsmen cross over for a single and this means WINDIES WILL BAT AGAIN.
Stuart Broad walks in at number 10, replacing Buttler. We could be in for some tailender slogging now.

OUT! Umpire's call it is and Buttler departs too! Holder is on a roll. He lands this on a good length in line of the stumps and Buttler is deep in his crease, trying to hop and work it to the leg side. He misses and is hit on the knee roll. Holder appeals, umpire Dharmasena thinks for a while and then raises his finger! Buttler takes the review and Hawk Eye shows it to be clipping the top of the bails! Unlucky for Buttler but such is the game... Three wickets for the captain now.
Another review. This time by England. Buttler has been adjudged LBW and he takes the review. Looks close...
On a length outside off, Buttler shoulders arms.
Full and around middle, nice inswing, watchfully defended.
Last hope for a miracle for England. Sam Curran arrives at number 9, replacing Foakes. He did that time and time again to the Indians recently. Can he repeat that against the West Indians?

OUT! Spectacular review from Holder and England have lost their 7th still being in the deficit! Excellent bowling. On a length outside off, Foakes looks to defend coming half forward but the ball comes back in prodigiously, beats the bat by a mile and hits him on the front pad. Roach roars an LBW shout but the umpire turns it down. To the naked eye, it seems like height is the factor. But Roach is confident and so is Holder. In fact, the captain instantaneously agrees to go for the review. Hawk Eye shows three reds and Foakes has to go!
Huge shout for LBW! Not given. Roach reckons that he has Foakes plumb in front. Holder gives his consent and the third umpire is called for again...
Wide outside off, left alone.

FOUR! Going for glory, getting greedy. A leg stump half volley now, Foakes just turns this delightfully over square leg for a boundary. Moves to 13 at run-a-ball with 12 of those coming in boundaries. The stand is worth 22 from just 21 deliveries.
Around off, more inward movement, watchfully blocked out.
Short leg comes in place now. With the ball going around like this, a bat-pad is always a chance...
Full and outside off, swinging in a long way, Foakes leans to defend but misses. The ball hits his back thigh and goes towards gully.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Well outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Consecutive boundaries. Overpitched, on middle, Buttler whips it over mid-wicket and gets a boundary.

FOUR! GLORIOUS! The deficit is now 9 and Buttler has become England's highest run scorer in this innings. Full and outside off, Jos drives it powerfully through mid off. The fielder gets across to his right, makes a half stop, but so powerfully is that hit that the ball still makes it to the fence behind.
Oohhh... on a good length around off, Jos shoulders arms again. Is hit right into the midriff.
Full and outside off, Buttler shoulders arms. The ball pitches and then moves a long way away.
OUCH! Rapped on the knuckles. Roach nods with a smile. Foakes acknowledges. Full and outside off, Ben looks to come forward and defend but gets hit on the right glove and then the forearm.
Big hooping inswinger, around off, Ben looks to work it to the leg side but misses and is hit on the pads.
Outside off, coming in, left alone.
FOUR! GORGEOUS! A looping half volley outside off, Foakes reaches out to this one and drives it through the vacant mid off region. The stand moves to 10 from 9 balls.
Landed outside off, left alone.
FOUR! A short ball, outside off, Foakes pulls it over mid-wicket and gets a boundary. 100 UP FOR ENGLAND. Trail by 17 now.
That ball has taken the inside edge onto the pads. They pick up a single.
Way outside off, let through.
Almost a replica of his first innings dismissal. A short ball, around middle, Foakes looks to pull but the ball takes the inside edge, hits his pads and then drops down.
Wide down the leg side, No trouble at all for the batsman.
Full and down the leg side, Buttler misses his flick and the ball goes off his pads through square leg. A leg bye taken.
Around off, solidly defended.
Ben Foakes comes in to bat now. He has not taken the field since that blow on his fingers on Thursday afternoon. Jason Holder comes to bowl as well. 8-2-27-2 so far.

OUT! BOWLED! Yet another one hits the stumps. Fourth bowled dismissal in this innings. Full and fast around off, coming in with the angle, Moeen looks to drive but like Stokes, he is playing for the away-going ball. Gets a thick inside edge which hits him on his pads and then the stumps. 23 runs still adrift...
Outside off, MA looks to play that with soft hands and the ball goes off the outside edge, but does not carry to first slip.
Landed outside off, fuller in length, Ali looks to defend but the ball goes past the outside edge. Late away movement.
FOUR! A bit streaky. Full and wide outside off, Moeen looks to drive but the ball swings away, takes the outside edge and sneaks behind point.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Full and well outside off, left alone.
Outside off, left alone.
FOUR! FLAMBOYANT! Full and wide outside off, Buttler leans and sends the ball flying through the covers. Not a soul moves. The deficit is now 27.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Around off, pushed towards point.
Good area from Gabriel, landing on a full length outside off, coming in, Buttler shoulders arms.
Full and outside off, Buttler looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Full and miles outside off, swinging away, left alone.
Moeen Ali walks in at number 7, replacing Stokes.

OUT! Dragged on! Number 5 is down. This is a poor, poor shot. They say, you live by the sword but you also die by it. Stokes was looking to counter-attack, trying to wipe off the deficit quickly but in that process, he has played one shot too many. Full and outside off, Ben plays for the outswinger but this one swings in. Catches the inside edge and rattles the leg stump. Stokes admonishes himself. The visitors need another 31 runs to make Windies bat again. Surely they can get past that?
Outside off, punched back to the bowler.
Whoa! Interesting. Out of nowhere, Stokes dances down the track, trying to disrupt the thought process of Roach. It is a length ball outside off, Ben lets it go.
Full and outside off, left alone.
The ball is too wide on the off side for the batsman to make any contact.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
A bouncer on middle, well ducked under.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Back of a length around off, solidly defended.
FOUR! Runs are lowing now. On a good length outside off, Buttler punches this through the covers and finds the gap.
A bouncer on middle, Jos ducks.

FIVE WIDES! Dear me... Gabriel has bowled this in the middle of the pitch and then the ball has deviated like a boomerang way down the leg side. Poor Shane Dowrich puts in an unbelievable dive to his left, but in vain.
Full and well outside off, left alone once more.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
FOUR! Cracking shot. Short and wide outside off, Stokes gets on top of the bounce and crashes it in front of point for a boundary!
Miles outside off, left alone.
Short and outside off, punched straight to point.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Kemar Roach to operate from the other end.
Full and wide outside off, driven straight to point.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
That ball has taken the inside edge onto the pads.

MIX-UP, CHANCE OF A RUN OUT, SAFE! Full and around middle, Buttler works it towards mid-wicket. Stokes is up and running for the single but Buttler is not so sure. He sends Stokes back who turns around and dives and would have made it even if the throw had found its mark.
Full and outside off, Buttler looks to defend but the ball whizzes past the outside edge.

Welcome back for what could be the final session of the match. 40 overs left in the day. Can Windies finish the game off by the end? The players slowly take the field. Buttler and Stokes get set to resume their fight. Shannon Gabriel will start off proceedings after Tea.
... DAY 3, FINAL SESSION ...

Hats off to Joseph. He has bowled his heart out. Roach and Gabriel were undisciplined but Holder and Joseph have bowled with fire and control. The final session could well be the final one of the match but we would love to see some fight from England and get a lead of around 100. Join us back at 3 pm local (1900 GMT).

Defining session of the Test match. 4 wickets in the span of 68 balls. Could have been 5 in the space of 70. But Stokes got a life. The Windies still look in firm control of this Test but at least Stokes and Buttler can try and offer some rearguard action.
Full and outside off, swinging away, let through. TEA ON DAY 3, ENGLAND TRAIL BY 44!
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Miles outside off, left alone.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full and down the leg side, Buttler looks to flick but misses. The ball goes off his pads through mid-wicket and a leg bye is taken.
Outside off, pushed towards point.
On middle and leg, flicked towards square leg for a run.
Landed outside off, JB gets across and then shoulders arms.
Good comeback by the bowler, landing it on a length outside off, Jos looks to defend but the ball pitches and curves off the seam to beat the outside edge.
FOUR! That is a cracking shot. Full and outside off, Buttler reaches out and drives it through mid off for a boundary!
Full and around off, pushed towards mid on.
Full and outside off, left alone.
Outside leg, left alone.
Full and outside off, Buttler drives it through mid off and gets another treble.
Full and around middle, driven straight back down the ground for three runs.
Down the leg side, Ben misses his flick.
Outside off, a play and a miss from Ben.
Full and down the leg side, flicked through mid-wicket for a couple.
Another ripper. This is a leg spinner! Full and outside off, Jos looks to defend but the ball hits a crack and then deviates away to beat the outside edge.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
A short ball around off, Buttler leaps to fend it off but the ball kicks off, hits his hand and then drops to the leg side.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and wide outside off, Buttler slashes hard but misses.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a couple.

EDGED, PUT DOWN! Alzarri would have had two in the over. A length ball, around off, Stokes looks to defend but gets a thick outside edge. It goes straight to John Campbell at third slip but he puts it down.

Another huge shout! The slip cordon is charging in but the umpire does not budge! On a length outside leg, Stokes looks to defend but misses. The ball hits something and goes behind. Like the Root dismissal, the entire slip cordon comes charging in. Again, Joseph does not react. Holder asks his slip fielders and Darren Bravo says he is not sure whether there was any edge. Holder is disappointed and does not take the review. No bat involved according to the replays.
A bouncer to greet the new man, Stokes ducks.
Ben Stokes comes in at number 6, replacing Denly.

OUT! Left alone and Denly has to walk back alone! Timberrrrrrr! No emotions from Joseph for obvious reasons. No reaction from Denly either. But the entire Windies team is pumped up. This 20-year old lad has just suffered a personal loss this morning. But instead of being with his family, he is here, playing for his national side. This is a ripper of a delivery. On a length outside off, Denly gets across but then shoulders arms. He trusts the line, trusts the bounce, perhaps expecting it to bounce over. But it doesn't. To his horror, he hears the sound which he does not want to hear. The ball rockets into the top of the off pole. 4 down are England and getting sucked into quicksand here...
Outside off, comes back in a long way, left alone. Superb movement.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
That is a beauty. On a length outside off, Buttler gets across to defend but the ball straightens after coming in initially, to beat the outside edge.
Full and around middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
Full again, well blocked out.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Around off, comes back in a long way, Denly falls over as he looks to work it to the leg side but manages to get it away for a couple.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, solidly defended.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Jos Buttler walks in at number 5, replacing his captain.

OUT! Caught behind! Wow. Superb review from Holder. He can do nothing wrong at the moment. The Midas of Windies cricket. A length ball outside off, Root looked to defend but the ball came back in a long way and hit the pads, on its way to the keeper. Now, there is no reaction from the bowler. But Holder comes charging in from first slip towards the umpire. Nothing from the bowler still. The captain looks at his slip cordon and then signals the 'T'. And yes, Snickometer shows a spike when the ball passes the glove. Root has to go! 35/0 has now become 56/3...
Is that gone? First an LBW appeal. Then one for caught behind. Neither given. Holder takes the review... He reckons there is wood on this...
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Outside off, punched behind point for a couple.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Around off, Denly looks to defend but misses and is hit on the pads. Holder appeals but that was too high.
Around middle and leg, the skipper looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. The ball drops to the leg side and they have taken a single.
Outside off, left alone.

FOUR! Oh nearly... Full and down the leg side, Root looks to flick but while doing so, falls over a bit. The ball hits the inner half of the bat and flies behind. So does Dowrich, to his left. But he cannot get there. The ball races to the fine leg fence. The deficit is now 66.
Outside off, pushed towards point.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Nips back in a long way, Denly looks to flick but misses. Is hit high on the pads and Joseph starts to appeal but then bails out. Height could have been an issue.
Tight line, outside off, watchfully pushed to the off side.
On a fuller length outside off, darts through, Joe defends it back onto the pitch.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
A short ball outside off, Denly looks to hook but misses.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Wide outside off, left alone.
Oh my... Holder has almost delivered the ball but Root bails out at the last possible moment. Jason is not happy even though Joe apologizes. Dead ball signalled.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
On a good length around off, stays low, Root looks to defend but gets a bottom edge.
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side.
Too full outside off, driven towards cover.
Fuller and wider outside off, not played at again.
Miles outside off, let through once more.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Landed outside off, coming in, left alone.
Cometh the hour, cometh the man. England would certainly love to believe that. They are in a whirlpool. The series seems to be stepping away. Need to catch it by the roots. And so comes Joe Root...

OUT! BOWLED! Holder has been trying and trying to get rid of Bairstow, nearly got him twice and on the third occasion, he strikes gold! Bairstow has come and Bairstow has gone. Suddenly, England are two down. Things are happening. A length ball outside off, Jonny plays a loose shot, trying to drive on the up but this is not that kind of a pitch! He misses the ball by a mile as it deviates back in, goes past the inside edge and cannons into the timber! England are still 70 adrift...
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads for a couple of runs.

MISSES THE STUMPS AGAIN! Flirting with danger, is Bairstow. Outside off, on a length, Jonny looks to back away and punch but is too close to the ball and gets a bottom edge, which just misses the stumps! Holder is furious.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Almost! On a length outside off, Bairstow looks to punch it but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads. So very nearly chopped it on.

FOUR! Well, that is well... unlucky for the bowler. The ball is nowhere close to the bat. It is pitched around middle and Bairstow is looking to work it to the leg side. But before the bat can come down at an angle, the ball is already through, off his pads, to the fine leg fence. Still, runs given.
DRINKS BREAK.
A very wide ball outside off to end the over, left alone.
A short ball outside off, JD hops to push it away.
Outside off, on a length, Joe feels for it but misses.
Around off, solidly defended.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Full and outside off, Denly plays that with a loose bottom hand, looking to drive but the ball seams back in, takes the inner half of the bat and goes towards short mid-wicket.
Alzarri Joseph into the attack now.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
FOUR! That is a bad ball. Short and outside off, sits up and asks to be smashed. Pulled behind square leg with disdain.
A length ball outside off, Bairstow looks to push but misses.
Outside off, left alone.
A short ball, around off, Bairstow immediately latches onto the pull and gets it through square leg for a couple.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Short and wide outside off, a slash and a miss.
Full and outside off, THAT STAYS LOW, Denly just about gets his bat down in time as he tries to defend.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.
Dropped short, pulled straight to square leg.
A bouncer on middle, Joe ducks.
A short ball outside off, Denly looks to pull but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Full on the pads, Bairstow flicks it towards square leg and gets off the mark with a couple.
On off, Jonny keeps it out.
Full length delivery on off, Bairstow defends it.
Slightly fuller than the previous one on off, Jonny defends it.
Length delivery outside off, Bairstow starts his innings carefully and leaves it alone.
Jonny Bairstow walks out at number 3.

OUT! Caught! There goes the first wicket. Holder has struck. He lands it on a length outside off and Rory looks to guide it behind point. However the ball lands on a crack and then deviates a mile in. Poor Burns is cramped for room and has nowhere to go. Cannot pull out of the shot, cannot play it cleanly. The ball takes the outside edge and goes straight to third slip where John Campbell takes it easily. Hard luck for Burns as he could not have done anything. England   still trail by 84.
Jason Holder is the first bowling change of the innings.
Good length delivery on off, Joe pushes it to point.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Denly sways away.
On middle and leg, Rory beautifully flicks it away to backward square leg. The fielder at fine leg covers the ground and gets there. Only a single taken.
Bouncer. Outside off, Rory ducks underneath it.
Slightly fuller on middle and off, Burns defends it.
Back of a length around off, Rory defends it to point.
Shorter in length, Joe leaves it alone and lets it go to the keeper.
Pulls back the length this time, Joe defends it.
FOUR! Exquisite! Full outside off, Denly gets on his front foot and drives it through covers for a boundary. Holds the pose for the photographers.
Full on middle and leg, Denly flicks it to mid-wicket and gets a brace.
Fuller length delivery on off, Joe defends it off his front foot.
Good length delivery outside off, Denly shoulders arms to it.
Once again, Gabriel is inconsistent with the line and sprays it down the leg side. Burns has no problem leaving it alone.
Shorter on length, Burns gets on top of the bounce and keeps it down with a straight bat.
Full around off, Burns taps it back to the bowler.
Down the leg side. It is back of a length. Rory leaves it alone.
On a length on off, Burns defends it by guiding the ball to point.
Length delivery outside off, Rory looks to defend it but the ball keeps low and he misses.
Good length delivery on off, Denly defends it to see off the over.
Back of a length delivery on off, it hits the inner half of Burns' straight bat and goes towards the on side. They steal a single.
Full outside off, Rory lets the keeper feel it.
Good length delivery on middle, the ball comes in with the angle. Burns plays it with soft hands and pushes it towards gully.
Slightly fuller outside off, Rory shoulders arms to it.
On a length on middle and leg, Denly hits it towards mid on and takes a single.
Good length delivery on off, Denly pulls it but once again his pull is not timed and hits him high on his bat. It goes uppishly towards the vacant mid-wicket region for a single.
Sprays this down the leg side. Joe looks to flick it but misses. Dowrich does well diving to his left.
FOUR! This should give Denly some confidence. Length delivery outside off, Denly cuts it through backward point for a boundary.
Back of a length delivery on middle, Joe defends it.
Good length delivery outside off, Denly chooses to leave it.

Beauty! Full length delivery on off, the ball jags back in and beats Denly who was looking to defend. It hits him on the back thigh pad. The players appeal but the umpire turns it down. They think about the review but don't take it.
Wide outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Down the leg side, Burns whips it behind square leg for a boundary!
A length ball wide outside off, Burns slashes hard but misses.
Full and around off, solidly defended.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. Two runs added to the total.
Down the leg side, helped through square leg for a single.

TOP EDGE, PUT DOWN! Gabriel is frustrated. A short ball, around off, Denly looks to pull but gets a top edge. The ball swirls in the air and Kraigg Brathwaite gets under it from fine leg but puts the catch down, trying to dive! A single taken.
That ball has struck the batsman on the thigh pad. The fielding side is asking the question. The umpire decides the batsman is not out.
A short ball outside off, Denly looks to pull but misses.
A length ball around middle, Denly looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Around off, defended from the crease.
Good length around middle, watchfully defended.
Gabriel to continue.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Landed outside off, let through.
Wide outside off, left alone.
FOUR! EDGED AWAY! On a length outside off, Burns looks to defend but the ball moves away, takes the outside edge and goes past second slip to the third man fence!
Outside off, a play and a miss.
Full and down the leg side, flick shot missed.

Welcome back. England get ready to resume what could be a marathon grit. Out come Denly and Burns. Probably, they need to take it hour by hour. If they can do what Brathwaite and Campbell did it for the Windies, put on an opening partnership of 70 or more, they will be right back in this Test match. Kemar Roach will start off proceedings after Lunch. Rory to face.
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

The 15-minute period has been negotiated safely by the English openers. Though, it would be fair to say that the bowling was not that great. It is not going to be easy to bat for long periods of time and the English resolve will be tested. Join us back at 12.40 pm local (1640 GMT).
Down the leg side, tucked towards fine leg for a single. LUNCH ON DAY 3, ENGLAND TRAIL BY 110!
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover.
A length ball, around middle, Rory allows it to seam away.
The batsman appears to have been struck on the thigh pad.
Another bouncer, ducked under again.
A bouncer outside off, Burns ducks.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

Huge, huge shout for LBW! Turned down! Lovely delivery. On a length outside off, Denly looks to defend with his bat around the off stump. But he is nowhere even close to blocking the ball. It nips back in, beats the bat comfortably and raps him on the pads. Roach appeals, appeals, appeals, then even extends his appeal. Dharmasena calmly waits for the appeal to quieten down and then shakes his head. Jason Holder charges from the slips towards his bowler, asking about the review but Roach smiles and says that perhaps it was missing leg. Holder looks at Dowrich and the keeper prevents him from taking the review. Hawk Eye confirms Roach's fears.
Down the leg side, Denly looks to flick but the ball goes off his thighs. Does not carry to Shimron Hetmyer at short leg.
Full and down the leg side, flicked towards fine leg for a single.
Outside off, lets this one go.
A length ball outside off, Burns gets down on a knee and plays it towards point.
Full and down the leg side, flick shot missed.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Outside off, left alone.

IN THE AIR... NO ONE TO CATCH IT! Brute of a delivery. Or let us rephrase it. First brute of the innings. A sharp bouncer, around middle, Burns is caught in no man's land as he looks to fend it off. But the ball takes the gloves, along with the handle and flies. Into the vacant square leg region. A single taken.
A bouncer, outside off, easily left alone.
On a good length around middle, worked uppishly, just wide of short leg!
Shannon Gabriel to share the new ball with Roach.
Full and down the leg side, Denly misses his flick. Very good keeping from Shane Dowrich as it is very difficult to collect balls in front of you.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground. One run added to the total.
Outside off, left alone.
A short ball, Burns leaps with the bounce and the ball nearly takes his head with it.
Outside off, let through to the keeper.
Legal ball now. First of the innings. Around off, solidly defended.

FIVE WIDES! Oh dear. Where did that come from? Pretty close to competing with the Steven Harmison from England during the 2006-07 Ashes. Remember that ball? First delivery of the match and Harmison bowled it outside the pitch. It went to Andrew Flintoff at first slip, it was that wide. Roach here, bowls this outside leg and the ball seams away through where first slip would have been for a right-hander. Poor Dowrich has no chance as he dives to his right. The ball races to the fine leg fence.
